Guided onboarding: generate config, sign up, connect project

## Usage

`circleci onboard [path] [flags]`

## Arguments

`<path>` is the directory to onboard. Defaults to the current directory.

## Flags

| Flag                           | Description                                                        |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--checkout-audience string`   | Audience of the bot's CircleCI checkout integration                |
| `--connection-audience string` | Audience of the bot's CircleCI connection integration              |
| `-H, --header stringArray`     | Request header for Forgejo, "Name: Value" (repeatable, max 10)     |
| `--no-browser`                 | Print the signup URL instead of opening a browser                  |
| `--org string`                 | Organization slug (e.g. gh/myorg) or UUID to set the project up in |
| `--owner string`               | Forgejo org or user that owns the repo (default: remote owner)     |
| `--provider string`            | Provider of a self-hosted remote: forgejo                          |
| `--provider-url string`        | Forgejo instance URL (default: https://<remote host>)              |
| `--repo-id string`             | Repository ID, if it cannot be resolved from the git remote        |
| `--scan`                       | Skip prompt: set up this repo on CircleCI                          |
| `--signup`                     | Skip prompt: sign up for CircleCI                                  |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- Set up the current directory (skip the choice prompt): 
  `circleci onboard --scan`
- Set up in a named org (required when you belong to several): 
  `circleci onboard --scan --org gh/acme`
- Connect a self-hosted Forgejo repo without prompts: 
  `circleci onboard --scan --provider forgejo --connection-audience u:1:ab12 --checkout-audience u:1:cd34`

## Details

Writes a starter config if none exists, creates and follows the project, adds a trigger.
